brief: Successor to W1-READABLES, which was killed mid-run by a container restart. The 73 quest reveals with no route: build the missing sources — ledgers, letters, environment reveals — route them through the existing reveal reader, and unblock Q-MAIN-06.
headline: THE SOURCES DID NOT EXIST, SO I MADE THEM. 26 documents written (9,769 words) and 25 marks put in the world as objects with positions, and the whole `environment` channel routed through one line in `CHANNEL_READERS` and one branch in `_takePropPending`. Demanded reveals with a route in play 58 -> 100 of 121; ledger 9 -> 28 of 28, letter 1 -> 7 of 7, environment 0 -> 16 of 16; quests with EVERY resolution blocked 2 -> 0. Proved in a browser: 4 of 4 legs walk to the thing, press interact at it, and watch the refusal go to zero, with two controls that bite; delete the reader on a copy of the tree and the same legs go 0 of 3. The main line played with the player's own verbs runs 5 -> 28 of 32 quests and the wall moves from Q-MAIN-06 to an exclusivity gate at Q-MAIN-29.
next_step: hand to a critic. NOT DONE and not faked: 21 demanded reveals still have no route and NONE of them is content this piece could write — 9 eavesdrop rows need a proximity-and-not-noticed reader against sim/stealth, 1 corpse row needs a search-a-body action, and 11 person rows name somebody who is in no file under game/data/npcs/**. 12 more document rows are unwritten and no resolution demands any of them; check-quests names all twelve. `mainline-chain-floor.mjs` still reports 0/40 and that is its allow-list, not the world — see THE CHAIN TOOL below.
notes: SUCCESSOR. W1-READABLES was `done` on disk at 58 of 121 routed. It wrote 9 documents, routed `ledger`/`letter` through `Engine._bookKnowledgeIndex()` and ruled on all 27 `environment` rows one by one. It did NOT write the remaining 26 document sources and built NO environment reader. That is this round, and its ruling file — reports/runs/W1-READABLES/environment-source-ruling.json — is where I started rather than re-deciding.

BEFORE, taken from the same tool at e97347f: `reveal-route-audit` section A = 58 of 121 routed, 63 with no route. ledger 9 of 28, letter 1 of 6, environment 0 of 18, book 5 of 5. Quests with EVERY resolution blocked: 2 (Q-MAIN-11, Q-MAIN-15). AFTER, at 0f5f456: 100 of 121, 21 with no route. ledger 28 of 28, letter 7 of 7, environment 16 of 16, book 6 of 6. Quests with every resolution blocked: 0.

WHERE THE CHANNEL COUNTS MOVED BY ONE. `letter` is 7 demanded not 6 and `environment` is 16 not 18 because two rows were AMENDED off the environment channel: Q-MAIN-05's `item_chapter_room_recension` is the chapter room's copy of the Recension whose ninth clause is in an ink that has not browned, and Q-LEDG-11's `letter_held_to_the_lamp` is two letters on one sheet of stock. Both are papers and the tell is ON the paper, so they are documents and are written as such. The predecessor's ruling reached the same verdict on both and I did not re-argue it.

THE OTHER 25 ENVIRONMENT ROWS ARE MARKS, and I disagree with the predecessor's split there — it put 4 of them in an `item` bucket wanting a separate item-examined reader. A lead disc on a crate wire with a ring pressed into it and no letters is a thing you look at that is standing somewhere, which is precisely what a mark is. Building a second reader for four rows would be the second mechanism this piece exists to avoid. They are marks.

FOUR SOURCES WERE SENTENCES AND NOT IDS — `the chalk on eleven doors`, `the cough on the lichen beds`, `the cut itself, on the shaded side`, `the stopper mark, matching the ones at the cut sapwell`. Amended to ids in the quest files, one line each, and the mark record carries the old sentence in its `provenance` so the amendment is readable rather than silent.

A FIFTH DATA DEFECT, FIXED WITH A JUDGEMENT DECLARED AS ONE. Q-XULA-05's `rev_court_ledger` declared `channel: ledger` with `source: ledgerer-hosk-vei`, which is a PERSON id; the last round reported it and refused to guess which half was wrong. The channel is right — the quest's truth is that the Drowned Court has four hundred years of counting that says so, which is a book and not a remark. So the SOURCE moved: `item_court_shortfall_series`, Hosk-Vei's own working series, written and placed in the archive he is posted in.

WHAT A MARK IS, because this is the whole of the new mechanism and it is small. `game/data/world/readables/site-marks.json` holds 25 records: an id (the reveal's `source`), a name, a place, and how it is drawn. `Engine._furnishInterior()` spawns the ones with `at.interior` into the room; `Engine._ensureProvinceMarks()` spawns the ones with `at.world` onto the heightfield, resolving `y` at spawn rather than authoring it. They are props — `takeable: false` — for the same reason an inscription is one: `listEntities()`, the reach prompt, `syncProps()`'s scene graph and the save round trip all take them without learning a new type.

NOTHING OPENS WHEN YOU LOOK AT A MARK, and the browser tool asserts it. `_takePropPending` calls `learnFrom('place', id)` and emits the input event; the UI mode is `world` before and `world` after on every leg. A panel saying that you notice the wax does not match is the narrator voice the register forbids, and it would also make the mark's own prose unnecessary. What the player reads is the NAME of the thing in the reach prompt — the verb is `look`, not `take` or `read` — and afterwards the journal entry the reveal row names, written by `note()`.

COUNTS ARE PART OF THE MODEL. Four of the marks carry `count` and `spread_m`: eleven chalked jambs at Stormhold, four unreachable kin-posts in the Helstrom gallery, four backed-up reaches above Mudwater, four damp returns on the Prefect's floor. The fact the player is being asked to learn IS the number, and one box standing for eleven doors is the same lie as printing the sentence.

THE ENGINE CHANGE IS FOUR ADDITIVE BLOCKS AND ONE CONSTANT. `CHANNEL_READERS` gains `environment: 'place'` (that is the router — `buildRevealRoutes` indexes `place:<id>` with no other change and `learnFrom` was already generic over `kind`); `spawnProp` gains a `site_mark` field; `_takePropPending` gains the mark branch; `_reachPrompt` gains the `look` verb; `_ensureProvinceMarks`/`_clearProvinceMarks`/`_siteMarksIn`/`_spawnMark` are new. No second index, no second reader, no fork of `reveal-routes.js`.

WHAT WAS WRITTEN. 26 documents, 9,769 words, `game/data/books/the-papers-in-evidence.json`, authored and placed by `tools/readables/mk-papers.mjs`. Blackrose's torn lease counterfoils, where the word `again` is written four times against the same twelve people and the fourth clerk rules the four hundred and eleven and initials it. The reconciled register with the destination column left out, and the copying clerk's working papers saying where all two hundred and six went. The gate-hand's nail-box of unsealed toll chits, where the count of chits agrees every day and the totals do not. The Legate's seal register, forty uses, thirty-nine of them stays. The Prefect's commission with `and shall not be renewed by silence` inserted at the Legate's direction and a date eight years old. The wharf's float book, kept in pencil because the shed is wet. A letter from a daughter at Soulrest asking whose hand is against her dead father's seat. The nine transfer applications, forwarded under the cover of the floor the applicant sits on.

PLACEMENT, and the rule is the last round's: a document lives in the room where the person who owns it stands, from `npc.post.at_building`. 26 placements across 12 rooms, one comment per room in `mk-papers.mjs`. ONE EXCEPTION, DECLARED: Q-XULA-02's coast survey line goes to the Helstrom gallery because Speaker Teel-Ashaan has no `post` in `game/data/npcs/**` at all — the same judgement round 1 recorded for `the-sap-and-the-knife`.

A REAL WORLD DEFECT MY OWN PLACEMENT CREATED, FOUND IN A BROWSER AND FIXED. `render/interior.js` allocated readable wall slots as `rSlots[(wi + 3 + ri * 2) % rSlots.length]`, which WRAPS — so a room with more documents than half its wall ring puts two of them within a metre of each other, and both the reach prompt and the interact reach take the NEAREST prop. Standing a metre from the tenth volume of the Tally in the Court archive and pressing the button OPENED THE BLACKROSE LEASE STUBS, because this round took that room from twelve documents to fifteen. Slots are now CHOSEN with a 2.6 m minimum separation, falling back to clear floor, and the browser leg that found it passes.

A SECOND WORLD DEFECT, IN MY OWN CODE, AND IT COST AN HOUR: `applyNamedState()` — which is what the harness `reset()` calls — runs `sim.reset()` (which replaces the props array) and THEN `_applyCell()`. A done-flag set before that boundary claims the marks are standing in a world where they are not, so every probe that called `reset()` saw zero marks in the whole province. The flag is only trusted now while at least one mark is actually in `sim.props`, and `_clearProvinceMarks()` takes them off the world when the cell stops being the province — without it the eleven chalked jambs of Stormhold stand inside the Helstrom undertemple.

PROVED IN THE RUNNING GAME. `tools/quests/mark-route-world.mjs`, report at reports/runs/W1-READABLES-R2/mark-route-world.json (gitignored like every run artifact). 4 legs run, 4 passed, all mainline. Q-MAIN-03 rev_shaft 2 -> 0, Q-MAIN-08 rev_the_ring 1 -> 0, Q-MAIN-11 rev_the_rhythm 2 -> 0, Q-MAIN-12 rev_wells_drink_the_overflow 2 -> 0. `knows` goes empty to [the reveal] on every one and the screen stays `world`. THE ONLY ACT IS `interact`, QUEUED THROUGH THE INPUT PIPELINE; the tool asserts against its own bytes that it never names `questReveal`, `questSetFlag`, `setWorldKnowledge` or `__ENGINE`.

CONTROLS, and both bit. (1) OUT OF REACH: same place, `reach_m` + 3 m, same button — learned nothing on all 4. (2) THE WRONG MARK: press at a different mark (another one in the same room, or the nearest other mark on the ground) — the refusal did not move on the 3 legs that had a sibling; the fourth says so rather than claiming a control it did not run. (3) A leg FAILS if the reveal was already known before the act, and FAILS if the gate did not refuse BY NAME beforehand.

THE BOOTSTRAP IS THE CHAIN, and it is why these legs are worth anything. Every mark case refuses at a cold start and the mainline ones refuse on a PREREQUISITE QUEST. So the tool plays the chain in front of the leg with the two verbs `viability-walk` allows itself plus the one thing this piece adds: it walks into the rooms and reads, and onto the ground and looks. Q-MAIN-12's leg therefore only exists because Q-MAIN-06 was unblocked by reading the Tally and Q-MAIN-11 by looking at the flooding road.

DELETE-THE-FIX, on a COPY of `game/` at `--entry <copy>/game/index.html` so nothing on the shared tree was perturbed (rule 17): `_takePropPending`'s mark branch disabled and the same four legs go 4 of 4 to 0 of 3. The two arms genuinely differ — with it, `knows` goes empty to [rev_the_rhythm] and refusals 2 -> 0; without it `knows` stays empty and refusals 2 -> 2 — and the fourth leg cannot even be REACHED, because Q-MAIN-12 is behind Q-MAIN-11 and Q-MAIN-11 can no longer be finished. Report at reports/runs/W1-READABLES-R2/mark-route-world-deletefix.json.

DELETE-THE-FIX 2 (the router), `reveal-route-audit --falsify no-router`: `revealRoutes` emptied and section E's 15 legs go 15/15 to 0/15, alongside section D's 37 to 0. DELETE-THE-FIX 3 (the placement half), `--falsify unmark`: forget all 25 mark placements and section A goes 100 -> 84 with `environment` 16 -> 0. `--falsify unplace` still moves the document half: 100 -> 59 with ledger, letter and book all to 0. All four arms are independent of each other.

SECTION E, NEW IN `reveal-route-audit.mjs`: the environment channel played through a real QuestEngine with no browser, the same shape as section D. 15 legs RUN (a leg only runs if the gate refused BY NAME before the act; a leg that ran and learned nothing is a FAILURE, not a skip), 15 pass. Section A.3 is the mark census — exists / stands nowhere / rejected by the placement rule.

THE HAND-FEED AT `mainline-chain-floor.mjs:234`, CHECKED BEFORE ANY CHAIN NUMBER WAS REPORTED, because the brief is right that it is this piece's own trap. `H.questReveal` occurs exactly once in that file, at line 260, inside `if (handFeedReveals)`, and `handFeedReveals` is false unless `--hand-feed-reveals` is passed. `H.learnTopic` occurs at 182-183 inside `if (sabotage === 'hand-feed')`. Nothing has replaced either. One thing IS unconditional and I am reporting it rather than leaving it for a critic: line 262 calls `H.questNote(step.id, ix)` for every journal index each step declares. It writes journal entries, which can seed `entry_topics` and therefore the OFFER gate; it cannot write a `know:` flag and so cannot feed a reveal. Not mine to change.

THE CHAIN TOOL THE BRIEF NAMES STILL REPORTS 0/40, and the honest reason is its allow-list. `mainline-chain-floor.mjs`'s verbs are creation, observation, `travelToGiver`, `questOpen`, `questResolve`, persuasion and the conversation verbs. There is no `enterInterior`, no `queueInputs`/`stepFrames`, no `teleport` — it cannot walk into a room and open a book or stand at a mark, so both channels this piece built are invisible to it exactly as `book` has been since W1-LIBRARY. All 40 signatures still stop at Q-MAIN-06 on `you do not know rev_the_curve_predates`. I did NOT widen somebody else's grant fence; that is what the fence is for.

SO THE CHAIN NUMBER IS TAKEN WITH A TOOL THAT CAN DO WHAT A PLAYER DOES, and it is three arms rather than the last round's two: `document-route-world.mjs --chain`, extended rather than forked. Same mainline order, same two verbs, TALKING HELD CONSTANT in all three, differing only in what the body may do when it arrives. NEITHER: 5 of 32, stops at Q-MAIN-06 on `res_the_number: you do not know rev_the_curve_predates` — the walk's own stop, reproduced, and it survives even with talking allowed, which is what makes it a control. READING ONLY: 10 of 32, stops at Q-MAIN-11 on `rev_the_rhythm` — round 1's number. READING AND LOOKING: 28 of 32, stops at Q-MAIN-29 with `closed by an earlier choice`, which is an exclusivity gate and not a missing route. Report at reports/runs/W1-READABLES-R2/document-route-chain.json.

Q-MAIN-06 UNBLOCKS, with numbers. In that chain the `neither` arm stops there and the other two walk past it; the mark tool's own bootstrap plays Q-MAIN-01 through Q-MAIN-11 by reading and looking, which is only possible because Q-MAIN-06's two `ledger` reveals now have documents in the archive under the burial stair. In section A, Q-MAIN-06's two demanded reveals are routed and the quest is no longer in the fully-blocked list, which went 2 -> 0.

NEW CONTENT CHECK, ARMED FAIL-CLOSED after the data existed (rule 13). `tools/check-quests.mjs` now FAILS THE COMMIT on an `environment` reveal whose mark is missing, names no place, sits outside its room's bounds, or stands within 4 m of the room's doorway — where `sim/settlement.js` takes `interact` for the way out first and the press can never reach it. Fail-closed rather than warning, unlike its document neighbour, and the difference is rule 13 and not taste: all 27 environment rows have a mark and every mark is placed, so it is silent on the shipped tree today. PROVED RED TWO WAYS on a copy of the tree: delete one mark, and move one mark to [0, 0.9, 4.2] in the Helstrom gallery. `--self-test` is 10/10 unchanged.

PROSE. `node tools/check-prose.mjs --verbose`: `game/data/books/the-papers-in-evidence.json` is `ok` on every gated metric at 9,769 words — questions, exclamations, sting, fragopen, andopen, contractions, and no tic. It was NOT ok on the first draft: 23 `-body` forms, zero questions, zero exclamations, zero contractions and andopen at 2.1 against a floor of 5.6. Every `-body` form was replaced with a concrete actor rather than with `-one`, which is what the tic list's own header asks for. Whole-run exit 0; the two red files in that run (`the-short-forms.json`, `told-and-sung.json`) are pre-existing and not mine.

A DEFECT IN A SHARED CHART TOOL, FOUND BY READING MY OWN PICTURE AND FIXED NARROWLY. Every glyph in `reveal-route-chart.mjs`'s font table is 23 characters and `text()` indexes it as `bits[j * 5 + i]` over seven rows of five, so the last two pixels of the fifth row of EVERY character are `undefined` and never drawn. On letters it is invisible; on digits it is not, and `28 OF 32` came out of the renderer reading `20 OF 30`. The ten digits are re-authored at full width under this round's flag ONLY, so the default stays `w1-19-r3` and the older pictures draw from the table they were drawn with. The other 37 glyphs carry the same truncation and re-authoring a font by eye is the tool owner's job. REPORTED HERE rather than fixed.

GATES at 0f5f456: boot-check PASS, check-data PASS (559 indexed files), check-content PASS (383 resolutions, none lost), check-quests PASS + self-test 10/10, check-prose exit 0, corpus-index exit 0, publish PASS (45 verdicts, all plotted). `reveal-route-audit` still exits 1 by design — it goes green only when EVERY demanded reveal has a route and 21 do not. It is not in INDEX.md's gate table and breaks no gate.

NO NEW SAVE FIELDS. A mark writes a `know:` flag into `q.quests[id].flags`, which `game/src/save/state.js` has always carried, and a document writes `sim.quest.booksRead`, which `game/data/save-manifest.json` already declares durable and id-sorted. Nothing new to round-trip, so rule 7 has nothing new to catch here.

TWO ARTIFACTS I TOUCHED THAT WERE NOT MINE, DECLARED. (1) `reports/runs/W1-READABLES/document-route-chain.json` was round 1's untracked run artifact and my first `--chain` run overwrote it before I noticed the default output path; round 1's numbers survive verbatim in its own status notes and the tool's default now points at `reports/runs/W1-READABLES-R2/`. (2) `reports/runs/W1-19-R3/reveal-route-audit.json` is regenerated by every run of the audit and now carries this round's numbers, which is that file's purpose. `docs/shots/2026-08-07-w1-19-r3-*.png` and `docs/shots/2026-08-07-w1-readables-*.png` are md5-identical to what they published.

CONTENTION AND LOAD, per rule 26. `node tools/contention.mjs --gate` returned exit 3 (WAIT) three times during this round and exit 0 twice. I DID PROCEED PAST EXIT 3 for the `mainline-chain-floor` run and the final `--chain` run, and I am saying so here because rule 21 requires it: the box was at 6-9 browser instances and 4.0-5.5 run queue per core. NO TIMING FIGURE IS QUOTED ANYWHERE IN THIS PIECE — every number is a count or a boolean and neither moves with load. One browser was launched and kept per run.

THE TREE MOVED UNDER ME REPEATEDLY. Fourteen agents are writing and the orchestrator's bank commits carried every file I wrote into c36653e, 9288ebf and 0f5f456 while I worked. Every number above was re-taken at 0f5f456 afterwards. I ran no `git add -A`.

OWNERSHIP. `redundant_with` names W1-READABLES, W1-18-r2, W1-19-r3 and W1-LIBRARY-r2 because this is the continuation of their finding on the same files, all `done`. The overlap with W1-03, W1-04-r2/r3, W1-06*, W1-12, W1-13-* and their critics is `game/src/engine.js` and `game/src/render/interior.js`, which most of this wave touches; my edits there are additive blocks plus one changed expression in the readable slot allocator, which no check pins and which was a real defect. I did not go near `game/data/dialogue/**`, which the sibling topic-graph piece owns.

NOT DONE, PLAINLY, AND NONE OF IT IS WRITEABLE CONTENT. 21 of 121 demanded reveals still have no route: 9 `eavesdrop` rows whose sources are real people but whose only conversation action is `talkTo`, which is walking up and being greeted — routing it there would give a player who introduced themselves credit for having listened unobserved; 1 `corpse` row with no search-a-body action to hang it on; and 11 person rows naming somebody who is in no file under `game/data/npcs/**` (clerk-meno, npc-ossei, npc-eleen, cutter-ashaan-hulei, npc-ineel-sa, npc-skara-hull-chalk, npc-ineve-corrano, npc-widow-tesla-vor, npc-ishi-vaal, npc-sorel-ithan, npc-river-band-elder). That last group is a cast list and is cheap. 12 further document rows are unwritten and NO resolution demands any of them; check-quests names all twelve every run.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. I did not build the eavesdrop reader, the corpse reader, or the missing NPC records. I did not widen `mainline-chain-floor.mjs`'s or `viability-walk.mjs`'s verb sets. I did not author `revealed_by[].journal` indices for any mark row, so looking at a mark writes the `know:` flag and no journal entry — the person channel does both and the environment channel does one, and the difference is 25 hand-picked indices nobody has chosen yet. I did not re-author the 37 non-digit glyphs of the chart font. I did not run `viability-walk.mjs`.
